correctness.rationale: Define three operators by row/column family membership and the existence of a Cartesian rectangle from the two upward-closed proper families. Forward mixing follows from upward closure. For the converse, if each minimal outer neighborhood is singleton then one good row yields a rectangle; if the inner family has a unique minimal member then it serves as a uniform witness across all good rows. Conversely, if a minimal outer neighborhood U has at least two points and the inner family has distinct minimal V0,V1, assign those two minimal sections on U and empty sections outside; any permitted rectangle would require its outer U exactly and inner neighborhood contained in V0∩V1, impossible by minimality. Repeat symmetrically. Count antichains with D_n−2 and inclusion-exclusion. The standalone checker exhaustively evaluates 529 local-family pairs and 175682 valuations across factor sizes 1 to 3; larger finite carriers are covered by proof, not experiment. Properness, finiteness, and nonempty carriers are indispensable hypotheses.

originality.rationale: The 2026 full-product work proves forward mixing in normal-filter semantics, where finite local filters are principal. The result here isolates precisely when the converse survives outside that normal subclass: singleton-generated outer or principal inner local antichains, in each order. Sano studies monotone bifactor products but without the third rectangle modality. Finite normal filters occupy the principal branch but do not dominate the nonnormal classification; existing Dedekind sequences give input counts, not this two-order incidence formula. Targeted searches identified no statement implying the complete nonnormal criterion or sharp two-order census. Remaining risk: alternate formulations as quantifier-interchange or hypergraph transversal results may cover it.
residual_risks: The local criterion could appear under quantifier-interchange, Boolean antichain, uniformization, or hypergraph-transversal terminology not surfaced by the searched records.
The computation only covers local carriers through three points; the arbitrary finite-size conclusion rests on the supplied combinatorial proof.
This review is not independent validation.

value.rationale: The rectangle-generated modality is an intrinsically motivated third operation in full neighborhood products. The issue is when iterated row-wise/column-wise witnesses can be uniformized to one rectangle after finite-intersection closure is dropped. The exact iff criterion and symmetric two-order obstruction fully classify this natural logic boundary. The two-parameter Dedekind census counts incidence between independently selected proper local neighborhood families, and the 3-by-3 obstruction threshold is sharp. This is a complete classification with a motivated separation from normal-filter products, not a numerical table recomputation or a routine parameter shift. Limited to finite proper local semantics, with no axiomatizability claims.
